🗓 **TAWG Daily Catch-up**
_2026-09-15 23:00 → 2026-09-16 23:00 UTC_

## ⚡ **Highlights**

> **Profile-commitment loop gains a reviewable seam** — Merlini's PR chaining both conformance ends was confirmed correct by a second reviewer, advancing it toward merge. [PR #42](https://github.com/trustless-ai/recompute-kit/pull/42)

> **Live-capital canary gap sparks conformance thread** — A real safety rail gap found during canary testing opened a focused discussion on TOCTOU-safe checks and admission separation, turning operational experience directly into conformance insight. [tg:tawg:4710]

> **Event-time and admission safety separated into new profile** — The thread's findings landed as a new conformance profile PR with explicit scope discipline, moving from conversation to filed implementation in a single window. [PR #45](https://github.com/trustless-ai/recompute-kit/pull/45)

## 🤝 **What moved**

### recompute-kit

_Two conformance PRs were filed and a multi-person discussion refined the safety primitives underlying both._

- Merlini (@gobross) **Opened** PR #42 to chain both ends of the profile-commitment loop into a single mechanical seam, giving the group a concrete reviewable artifact for the commitment-loop closure. [PR #42](https://github.com/trustless-ai/recompute-kit/pull/42)

- Pavlo **Confirmed** on PR #42 that the composition logic and computed seam look correct, providing the verification signal needed for the PR to move forward. [comment on PR #42](https://github.com/trustless-ai/recompute-kit/pull/42#issuecomment-5697251076)

- Baby Blue Viper (@babyblueviper1) **Surfaced** a per-cell safety rail gap found on a live-capital canary and brought it to the group as an open conformance question, connecting real operational experience to the gate-work conversation. [tg:tawg:4710]

- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Bridged** the canary gap to an existing analogue in pq-recovery-classes-v0, where a key property had already been separated from auditor-snapshot state, showing the pattern was already partially in scope. [tg:tawg:4711]

- Baby Blue Viper (@babyblueviper1) **Named** the TOCTOU dependency precisely: the per-close check is only safe because of the admission separation, making the implicit safety assumption explicit and actionable for the group. [tg:tawg:4712]

- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Located** the structural shape in captured-admission-v0, confirming that request-vs-sequence identity separation already exists there while noting the full concurrency primitive is absent, pinpointing exactly what remains to be built. [tg:tawg:4715]

- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Shipped** PR #45, turning the thread's event-time vs. concurrency insight into a standalone conformance profile that mechanically separates periodic-pass from event-time authorization with explicit scope limits. [tg:tawg:4719]

- Baby Blue Viper (@babyblueviper1) **Validated** PR #45 by reading it directly and calling out the disciplined scope boundary — the explicit non-claim on production CAS and live exactly-once semantics — as the most valuable aspect of the design. [tg:tawg:4720]

### cross-reference-console

_The registry index moved forward with a routine automated update._

- The automated watcher pushed a registry watermark update covering new claims entries, keeping the cross-reference index current for downstream verification work. [commit 268c77b](https://github.com/trustless-ai/cross-reference-console/commit/268c77b795aef5f13b018e76e4f7d9307a81b395)

## 🚀 **Next up**

### 💡 **Ideas to follow**

- Whether the missing full concurrency primitive could be drafted as a follow-on profile to PR #45, completing the shape already present in captured-admission-v0
- How the TOCTOU-safe per-close check pattern might generalize across other live-capital gate profiles

### ✅ **TODOs**

- Review and merge PR #42 now that its composition logic has been confirmed correct
- Review PR #45's scope boundary and consider whether the explicit non-production-CAS discipline should become a shared conformance convention

## 🤖 **Trusty's take**

> **Today's spark:** A real canary deployment flagged a safety gap, the group traced it through existing profiles, surfaced the TOCTOU dependency by name, and closed the session with a new conformance profile PR filed and peer-validated — discovery to implementation in a single window.
>
> When the canary chirps and the whole group follows the sound all the way to a filed PR, that is the spec-to-code relay working exactly as designed 🎯
